Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

indicate verb

also be a sign of, point to, make clear, point out, make known

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre
Traupman 247, 332: significāre, indicate
Traupman 332

significō, significāre, significāvī, significātum

verb, first conjugation

indicate, show, make known

Lewis & Short: “to show by signs; to show, point out, express, publish, make known, indicate”; with an accusative and infinitive when a letter or a sign shows that something is so. Of a word, “mean” (see mean).

Other words

  • indicō, indicāre, indicāvī, indicātum — point out, be a sign of; reveal

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Publil. Sent. I 43: Inertia indicātur, cum fugitur labor.; Publil. Sent. P 61: Parātae lacrimae īnsidiās, nōn flētum indicant.; Traupman 30; Traupman 27

    First conjugation, with a short i; not indīcō, indīcere, proclaim.

  • dēmōnstrō, dēmōnstrāre, dēmōnstrāvī, dēmōnstrātum — point out (as with a finger), show

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Catull. 55.1–2: dēmōnstrēs ubi sint tuae tenebrae

  • palam facere — make known, make public

    also used · classical · Traupman 337

Examples

  • significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre et esse fortem virum et cōnstantem

    for they showed that you are now bearing your military service with a steady mind, and are a brave and steadfast manCic. Fam. 7.18.1

  • Parātae lacrimae īnsidiās, nōn flētum indicant.

    Tears at the ready indicate a trick, not grief.Publil. Sent. P 61

See also sign, show, mean.
